title: Arakhin 27
description: Chapter 7, Ein Makdishin, closes with why priests and Levites “may always consecrate”, and chapter 8, HaMakdish Sadehu, opens with the bidding to redeem a consecrated field: the owner opens first because he adds a fifth, the man who bid an issar or an egg, bidders who renege one after another or all at once, and how much the owner must pay to outbid another.
topics: 📜 “Which is not of his ancestral field”: the extra “of” for Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon
🧑‍⚖️ Priests and Levites “may always consecrate”: taught only because of the first clause
📖 Hadran: chapter 7, Ein Makdishin, ends; chapter 8, HaMakdish Sadehu, begins
🔨 “You open first”: the owner adds a fifth, the field is dear to him, and the mitzva of redemption is his
🥚 An issar or an egg: redeeming with something whose fifth is not worth a peruta
↩️ Bidders who renege: one after another, or all at once and they divide the loss (Rav Ḥisda)
➕ The owner bids twenty, another bids more: twenty-six, twenty-seven … thirty, and “a man has come in my place”
⚖️ Second tithe versus consecrated property, and Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on a fifth for the other’s addition

a1.he: וְהָכָא קְרָא אַשְׁכֻּחַ וּדְרֻשׁי: לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״אִם מִשְּׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּתוֹ״, אִי נָמֵי: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה״, מַאי ״מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״? שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ רְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה, יָצְתָה זוֹ שֶׁרְאוּיָה לִהְיוֹת שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.

a2.he: הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם מַקְדִּישִׁין לְעוֹלָם וְכוּ׳. בִּשְׁלָמָא גּוֹאֲלִין אִצְטְרִיךְ, לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּיִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָא פָּרְקִי אֶלָּא עַד יוֹבֵל, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּכֹהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם גּוֹאֲלִין לְעוֹלָם. אֶלָּא מַקְדִּישִׁין, מַאי אִירְיָא כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם? אֲפִילּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי!

a3.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל עַצְמָהּ, הָנִיחָא לִשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמַר: ״בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל עַצְמָהּ לָא קָדְשָׁה״, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּכֹהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם מַקְדִּישִׁין לְעוֹלָם, אֶלָּא לְרַב, מַאי אִירְיָא כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם? אֲפִילּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי!

a4.he: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל בֵּין לְאַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל לְמָה לִי? אֶלָּא, אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל וּלְאַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל״, תְּנָא סֵיפָא נָמֵי ״בֵּין לְאַחַר הַיּוֹבֵל בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל״.

a5.he: וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא רֵישָׁא ״אֵין מַקְדִּישִׁין וְלֹא גּוֹאֲלִין״, תְּנָא נָמֵי סֵיפָא ״מַקְדִּישִׁין וְגוֹאֲלִין״.

a7.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֵין הַיּוֹבֵל, אוֹמֵר לוֹ: ״פְּתַח אַתָּה רִאשׁוֹן״, שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ, וְכׇל אָדָם אֵין נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ.

a8.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ מִפְּנֵי רָעָתָהּ, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: פְּתַח אַתָּה רִאשׁוֹן. אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּאִיסָּר. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא אָמַר זֶה ״בְּאִיסָּר״, אֶלָּא ״בְּבֵיצָה״, שֶׁהֶקְדֵּשׁ נִפְדֶּה בְּכֶסֶף וּבְשָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף, אָמַר לוֹ: ״הִגַּעְתִּיךָ״, נִמְצָא מַפְסִיד אִיסָּר וְשָׂדֵהוּ לְפָנָיו.

a9.he: גְּמָ׳ הַמַּקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ בְּשָׁעָה כּוּ׳. אוֹמְרִין? וְהָתַנְיָא כּוֹפִין! מַאי ״אוֹמְרִין״ נָמֵי? כּוֹפִין. וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: מֵעִיקָּרָא אוֹמְרִין, אִי צָאֵית — צָאֵית, וְאִי לָא — כּוֹפִין.

a10.he: שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ וְכוּ׳. מַאי אִירְיָא שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ? תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּאַיְּידֵי דַּחֲבִיבָה עֲלֵיהּ טָפֵי וּפָרֵיק לַהּ! וְעוֹד, מִצְוַת גְּאוּלָּה בָּאָדוֹן!

a11.he: חֲדָא וְעוֹד קָאָמַר, חֲדָא: דְּאַיְּידֵי דַּחֲבִיבָה עֲלֵיהּ טָפֵי וּפָרֵיק לַהּ, וְעוֹד: מִצְוַת גְּאוּלָּה בָּאָדוֹן הִיא, וְעוֹד: שֶׁהַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין חוֹמֶשׁ כּוּ׳.

a12.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ וְכוּ׳. לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף כְּכֶסֶף, וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף אֵינוֹ כְּכֶסֶף.

a13.he: וְהָא קַיְימָא לַן, דְּשָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף כְּכֶסֶף! דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא שָׁוֶה כֶּסֶף כְּכֶסֶף, וְהָכָא בְּפוֹדִין בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין בְּחוּמְשׁוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה קָמִיפַּלְגִי. תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר: אִיסָּר, דְּאִיכָּא בְּחוּמְשׁוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה — פָּרְקִינַן, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כְּבֵיצָה נָמֵי פָּרְקִינַן.

a14.he: אָמַר לוֹ: ״הִגַּעְתִּיךָ״, נִמְצָא מַפְסִיד אִיסָּר וְשָׂדֵהוּ לְפָנָיו. סְתָמָא כְּרַבָּנַן.

a15.he: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר אֶחָד: ״הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים״, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים״, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים״, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בְּאַרְבָּעִים״, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בַּחֲמִשִּׁים״. חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר. חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל אַרְבָּעִים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר.

a16.he: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל שְׁלֹשִׁים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר, חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל עֶשְׂרִים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר, חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר — מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּשׇׁוְויוֹ, וְנִפְרָעִין מִשֶּׁל עֶשֶׂר אֶת הַמּוֹתָר.

a17.he: הַבְּעָלִים אוֹמְרִים בְּעֶשְׂרִים, וְכׇל אָדָם אוֹמְרִים בְּעֶשְׂרִים — הַבְּעָלִים קוֹדְמִין, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵם מוֹסִיפִין חוֹמֶשׁ. אָמַר אֶחָד: ״הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַחַת״ —

b1.he: הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין עֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ, ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁתַּיִם״ — הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין עֶשְׂרִים וָשֶׁבַע,

b2.he: ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְשָׁלֹשׁ״ — הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁמוֹנֶה, ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע״ — הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין עֶשְׂרִים וָתֵשַׁע, ״בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ״ — הַבְּעָלִים נוֹתְנִין שְׁלֹשִׁים, שֶׁאֵין מוֹסִיפִין חוֹמֶשׁ עַל עִלּוּיוֹ שֶׁל זֶה.

b3.he: אָמַר אֶחָד: ״הֲרֵי שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ״, אִם רָצוּ הַבְּעָלִים לִיתֵּן שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד וְדִינָר — הַבְּעָלִים קוֹדְמִין, וְאִם לָאו — אוֹמֵר לוֹ: ״הִגַּעְתִּיךָ״.

b4.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁבֶּן אַרְבָּעִים עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.

b5.he: אֲבָל אֵין בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים עוֹמֵד בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, מְשַׁלְּשִׁין בֵּינֵיהֶן.

b6.he: תְּנַן: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל אַרְבָּעִים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין עַד עֶשֶׂר. אַמַּאי? לִיתֵּן בַּר חַמְשִׁין בַּהֲדֵיהּ! דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן חֲמִשִּׁים.

b7.he: חָזַר בּוֹ בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר, אַמַּאי? וְלִיתֵּן דְּבֶן אַרְבָּעִים בַּהֲדֵיהּ! דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן אַרְבָּעִים. חָזַר בּוֹ בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים — מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר, אַמַּאי? לִיתֵּן דְּבֶן שְׁלֹשִׁים בַּהֲדֵיהּ! דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים.

b8.he: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר, מוֹכְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּשׇׁוְיָהּ וְנִפְרָעִין מִשֶּׁל עֶשֶׂר אֶת הַמּוֹתָר, לִיתֵּב דְּבֶן עֶשְׂרִים בַּהֲדֵיהּ! וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי דְּלֵיכָּא בֶּן עֶשְׂרִים, אִי הָכִי, ״נִפְרָעִין מִשֶּׁל עֲשָׂרָה״ — ״נִפְרָעִין מִמֶּנּוּ״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!

b9.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בְּבַת אַחַת, כָּאן בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה. תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: חָזְרוּ כּוּלָּן כְּאֶחָד — מְשַׁלְּשִׁין בֵּינֵיהֶם. וְהָא אֲנַן תְּנַן: מְמַשְׁכְּנִין מִנְּכָסָיו עַד עֶשֶׂר! אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

b10.he: אִיכָּא דְּרָמֵי לְהוּ מִירְמָא: תְּנַן: חָזַר בּוֹ שֶׁל עֶשֶׂר, מוֹכְרִין אוֹתָהּ בְּשׇׁוְיָהּ וְנִפְרָעִין מִשֶּׁל עֶשֶׂר אֶת הַמּוֹתָר, וְהָתַנְיָא: מְשַׁלְּשִׁין בֵּינֵיהֶם! אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן — בְּבַת אַחַת, כָּאן — בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה.

b11.he: הַבְּעָלִים אוֹמְרִים בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְכׇל אָדָם בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְכוּ׳. לְמֵימְרָא דְּחוֹמֶשׁ עֲדִיף? וּרְמִינְהוּ: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אוֹמֵר בְּסֶלַע, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּסֶלַע וְאִיסָּר — שֶׁל סֶלַע וְאִיסָּר קוֹדֵם, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמּוֹסִיף עַל הַקֶּרֶן!

b12.he: הָכָא דְּחוּמְשָׁא רַוְוחָא דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ הוּא — חוֹמֶשׁ עֲדִיף, הָתָם דְּחוּמְשָׁא רַוְוחָא דְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת — קַרְנָא תִּיפְרוֹק שַׁפִּיר, חוּמְשָׁא לָא אִיכְפַּת לַן.

b13.he: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי הוּא שֶׁלִּי כּוּ׳. בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ נוֹתְנִין שְׁלֹשִׁים. וְלֵימְרוּ הַבְּעָלִים: אֲתָא גַּבְרָא בַּחֲרִיקִין! דַּאֲמוּר בְּעָלִים דִּינָר.

b14.he: וְלִיתְנֵי דִּינָר! לָא דָּק. וְלָא? וְהָא קָתָנֵי: אִם רָצוּ הַבְּעָלִים לִיתֵּן שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד וְדִינָר — בְּעָלִים קוֹדְמִין! אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: דַּאֲמוּר בְּעָלִים פְּרוּטָה, וְלָא דָּק.

b15.he: שֶׁאֵין מוֹסִיפִין חוֹמֶשׁ עַל עִלּוּיוֹ כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא נִישּׁוֹם הֶקְדֵּשׁ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה, אֲבָל נִישּׁוֹם הֶקְדֵּשׁ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה — מוֹסִיפִין.

b16.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מוֹסִיפִין, וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מוֹסִיפִין. הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִי לָא נִישּׁוֹם, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי? אֶלָּא דְּנִישּׁוֹם.

b17.he: לֵימָא רַב חִסְדָּא דְּאָמַר כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי? לְעוֹלָם דְּלָא נִישּׁוֹם, וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי מַחְמִירִין.

b18.he: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם דְּנִישּׁוֹם, וְאֵיפוֹךְ — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מוֹסִיף. וְלִיתְנְיַהּ גַּבֵּי קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל! אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם דְּלֹא נִישּׁוֹם, וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי מַחְמִירִין.

b19.he: אָמַר אֶחָד: הֲרֵי הִיא שֶׁלִּי בְּעֶשְׂרִים וָשֵׁשׁ כּוּ׳. רָצוּ — אִין, לֹא רָצוּ — לָא.

b21.he: וְדִינָר מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ? אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָכִי קָאָמַר, אִם רָצוּ בְּעָלִים מֵעִיקָּרָא לִיתֵּן חֶשְׁבּוֹן הַמַּגִּיעַ לְאֶחָד וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וְדִינָר;

messages.text: Continued from 26b: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon, too, hold that acquiring a field for its produce is like acquiring the field itself, so they too need the verse for a son whose father died before he consecrated the field. He goes on:

But here, with regard to their opinion that even if the son consecrated the field before his father’s death it is considered an ancestral field, this is because they found another allusion in the verse and interpreted it as follows:

notes.he: דהקדישה ואח"כ מת אביו תיהוי אחוזה דאל"כ דלא רבי לן קרא אלא מת אביו ואח"כ הקדישה ניכתוב קרא אשר לא אחוזתו ומתרביא הא דר' מאיר דדריש יצתה זו שהיא כבר אחוזה:
notes.en: And here they found another verse and expounded it: that if he consecrated it and afterward his father died, it is an ancestral field. For otherwise, if the verse included for us only [the case where] his father died and afterward he consecrated it, let the verse write “which is not his ancestral field,” and Rabbi Meir’s [ruling] would be included [by it], since he expounds: excluding this one, which is already an ancestral field.

notes.he: דיצאת זו שראויה להיות שדה אחוזה ולאו משום טעמא דקנין פירות לא כקנין הגוף דמי:
notes.en: They found and expounded: that this one, which is due to become an ancestral field, is excluded; and not for the reason that acquisition of the produce is not like acquisition of the body.

messages.text: If the verse meant to indicate only the halakha that Rabbi Meir derives from it, let the Merciful One write: And if he will consecrate unto the Lord a field that he has bought, which is not his ancestral field, or: Which is not an ancestral field. What is the meaning of the extra word “of” in the phrase: “Which is not of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:22)? It teaches that only a field that is not due to become his ancestral field is treated like a purchased field, thereby excluding this field, which is due to become his ancestral field.

verse.he: וְאִם אֶת־שְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ אֲשֶׁר לֹא מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ יַקְדִּישׁ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: If one consecrates to GOD land that was purchased, which is not one’s land-holding,

notes.he: ש"מ לכדאמרינן למדרש הקדישה ואח"כ מת אביו:
notes.en: Why do I need “of the field”? Conclude from it what we said: to expound [the case where] he consecrated it and afterward his father died.

notes.he: שבשעת הקדש היתה ראויה להיות שדה אחוזה:
notes.en: Excluding this one: which at the time of consecration was due to become an ancestral field.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: The priests and the Levites may always consecrate their ancestral fields and may always redeem their ancestral fields, both before the Jubilee Year and after the Jubilee Year.

Granted, the mishna’s statement that they may always redeem their ancestral fields was necessary, in order to exclude them from the halakha that applies to the ancestral field of an Israelite, which may be redeemed only until the Jubilee Year, and if not redeemed by then, it is given to the priests. In contrast, the mishna teaches us that priests and Levites may always redeem their fields.

notes.he: אפי' בשנת היובל:
notes.en: That it teaches us that priests and Levites redeem always: even in the Jubilee Year.

messages.text: But with regard to the statement that they may always consecrate their fields, why does the mishna specifically mention priests and Levites? Even an Israelite may always consecrate his field, both before and after the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: דהא תניא בריש פירקין (ערכין דף כד.) מקדישין לפני היובל וכו' (ואי משום דקתני מתני' אין מקדישין פחות משתי שנים לפני היובל הא אוקימנא (שם) דעצה טובה קמ״ל):
notes.en: Even an Israelite too: for it is taught at the beginning of our chapter (Arakhin 24a): one may consecrate before the Jubilee, and so on. (And if it is because our mishna teaches that one may not consecrate less than two years before the Jubilee, we established there that it teaches us good advice.)

messages.text: And if you would say that the mishna means that priests and Levites may consecrate their fields during the Jubilee Year itself, whereas an Israelite may not, this works out well according to the opinion of Shmuel, who says (24a) that if an Israelite consecrated his field during the Jubilee Year itself it is not consecrated. Accordingly, the mishna teaches us that priests and Levites may always consecrate their fields, even in the Jubilee Year itself.

notes.he: גבי ישראל לא קדשה אצטריך לאשמועי' דגבי כהנים קדשה:
notes.en: This works out well according to Shmuel, who says: with an Israelite it is not consecrated; [so] it was necessary to teach us that with priests it is consecrated.

messages.text: But according to the opinion of Rav, why does the mishna specifically mention priests and Levites? Even an Israelite may consecrate his field during the Jubilee.

notes.he: ליכא למימר הכי דמהיכא תיתי לן מקראי:
notes.en: But according to Rav: one cannot say this, for from where in the verses would we come to it?

messages.text: And according to your reasoning, one may similarly ask: Why do I need the statement that priests and Levites may consecrate their fields both before the Jubilee Year and after the Jubilee Year? Doesn’t the mishna already state that they may always consecrate their fields?

Rather, since the tanna taught in the first mishna in this chapter (24a) that Israelites may not consecrate their fields less than two years before the Jubilee and they may not redeem them less than one year after the Jubilee, the tanna also taught in the latter mishna that priests and Levites may consecrate their fields both after the Jubilee and before the Jubilee, despite the fact that there is no novelty in this statement.

notes.he: ישראל תנא סיפא גבי לוים:
notes.en: Since he taught in the first clause: [the case] of an Israelite, he taught in the latter clause [the case] of Levites.

notes.he: אמר לך רב ולטעמיך כיון דבשנת יובל עצמה הקדיש ש"מ בין לפני יובל ובין לאחר יובל ולמה לי למיתנייה אלא איידי דתנא רישא דמתניתין אין מקדישין לפני יובל ולא גואלין אחר יובל פחות משנה תנא נמי סיפא בין לפני יובל וכו' ואיידי דתנא אין מקדישין [ולא גואלין תנא נמי סיפא מקדישין] וגואלין ולעולם מקדישין לא אצטריך למתני אלא גואלין איצטריך כדאמר ואיידי דתני גואלין לעולם תנא מקדישין לעולם:
notes.en: Rav would say to you: And according to your reasoning, since he may consecrate in the Jubilee Year itself, conclude [that he may] both before the Jubilee and after the Jubilee; so why do I need to teach it? Rather, since he taught in the first clause of the mishna: one may not consecrate before the Jubilee, and may not redeem after the Jubilee, less than a year, he also taught in the latter clause: both before the Jubilee, and so on. And since he taught “one may not consecrate [and may not redeem],” he also taught in the latter clause “they consecrate and redeem.” And in truth, “they consecrate always” did not need to be taught; only “they redeem” was needed, as stated; and since he taught “they redeem always,” he taught “they consecrate always.”

messages.text: And similarly, since the tanna taught in the first mishna that Israelites may neither consecrate their fields less than two years before the Jubilee nor redeem them less than one year after the Jubilee, the tanna also taught in the latter mishna that priests and Levites may always consecrate and redeem their fields, despite the fact that there is no novelty with regard to consecrating in this statement either, as Israelites may also consecrate their fields both after the Jubilee and before the Jubilee.

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.text: הדרן עלך אין מקדישין · Hadran alakh Ein Makdishin: we will return to you, chapter 7, “One May Not Consecrate [an Ancestral Field Less Than Two Years before the Jubilee].”
Chapter 8 · המקדיש שדהו · HaMakdish Sadehu: one who consecrates his field at a time when there is no Jubilee, the bidding to redeem a consecrated field, and then dedications [ḥaramim] of property.
Mishna

In the case of one who consecrates his ancestral field during a period when the Jubilee Year is not observed, and therefore the field is not redeemed according to a fixed rate of fifty shekels per beit kor but according to its value, when the treasurer announces the sale of the field he says to the owner: You open the bidding first; how much do you offer for its redemption?

notes.dh: מתני' המקדיש שדהו בשעה שאין היובל
notes.he: בזמן שאין היובל נוהג:
notes.en: Mishna. One who consecrates his field at a time when there is no Jubilee: at a time when the Jubilee is not in effect.

notes.he: בכמה אתה רוצה לפדותה ומפני ריוח של הקדש שואלין לו תחלה:
notes.en: You open first: for how much do you want to redeem it? For the sake of the Temple’s profit, they ask him first.

notes.dh: מתני' המקדיש שדהו בשעה שאין היובל נוהג
notes.he: פירוש בזמן שאין היובל נוהג דאז הוא נפדה בשוייו ויש בו ריוח להקדש לפתוח תחלה הבעלים מפני החומש אבל בזמן שהיובל נוהג הוא נפדה לפי זרעו בנ' סלעים בית זרע חומר שעורים ובשדה אחוזה מיירי ובזמן הבית מיירי דאיכא רווחא להקדש דאי שלא בזמן הבית מחללו אם ירצה אפי' לכתחלה על שוה פרוטה לפי שאין בו ריוח להקדש דלאיבוד אזיל כדאיתא לקמן בסוף פירקין (ערכין דף כט.) ההוא דאחרים לנכסיה אתא לקמיה דרב יהודה א"ל שקול ד' זוזי אחיל עלייהו ושדינהו בנהרא ולישתרי לך וא"ת היאך נמצא בזמן שאין היובל בזמן הבית י"ל בזמן שגלו ישראל דבעינן כל יושביה עליה:
notes.en: Mishna. One who consecrates his field at a time when the Jubilee is not in effect: meaning, at a time when the Jubilee is not in effect, for then it is redeemed at its value, and there is profit for the Temple in having the owners open first, because of the fifth. But at a time when the Jubilee is in effect it is redeemed according to its seed: fifty sela for the area sown with a ḥomer of barley. And it speaks of an ancestral field, and of the time of the Temple, when there is profit for the Temple. For if not in the time of the Temple, one may desacralize it, if he wishes, even ab initio, onto the equivalent of a peruta, since there is no profit in it for the Temple, as it goes to waste; as is found below at the end of our chapter (Arakhin 29a): a certain man who devoted his property came before Rav Yehuda; he said to him: Take four zuz, desacralize [the property] onto them, throw them into the river, and it will be permitted to you. And if you ask: how can there be a time with no Jubilee in the time of the Temple? One can say: at the time when [some of] Israel were exiled, for we require “all its inhabitants upon it.”

notes.he: להמקדיש בשעה שמכריזין אותה לפדותה [אומר לו לבעלים] פתח אתה ראשון בכמה אתה רוצה לפדותה לפי שאם לא ימצא מי שירצה לפדותה ביוקר מן הבעלים מוטב שיפדנה הבעלים משום ריוח דהקדש לפי שהבעלים מוסיפין חומש על פדיונן:
notes.en: He says to him: to the one who consecrated, when they announce it for redemption, [he says to the owners]: You open first; for how much do you want to redeem it? For if no one is found who wants to redeem it for more than the owners, it is better that the owners redeem it, for the Temple’s profit, since the owners add a fifth onto their redemption.

messages.text: This method is advantageous for the Temple treasury, as the owner gives an additional payment of one-fifth of the value of the field, and every other person does not give an additional one-fifth payment.

notes.he: ולהכי נקט בשעה שאין היובל נוהג דבזמן שנוהג אין צריך לשואלו בכמה תפדנה שהרי דמיה קצובין בית כור בנ' סלע ובשדה אחוזה קא מיירי ובזמן שאין יובל נוהג נפדית בשוייה כדתניא בשילהי פירקין אין שדה אחוזה נוהג אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג:
notes.en: As the owners give a fifth: and that is why it specified “at a time when the Jubilee is not in effect.” For at a time when it is in effect there is no need to ask him for how much he will redeem it, since its price is fixed: a beit kor for fifty sela. And it is speaking of an ancestral field; and at a time when the Jubilee is not in effect, it is redeemed at its value, as it is taught at the end of our chapter: [the law of] an ancestral field applies only at a time when the Jubilee is in effect.

messages.text: There was an incident involving one who consecrated his field due to its inferior quality. The treasurers said to him: You open the bidding first. He said: It is hereby mine for an issar, a small sum.

notes.he: שהיתה יציאתה מרובה על השבח:
notes.en: Due to its inferior quality: its expenses were greater than its yield.

notes.he: או מפני שהיה מס שלה מרובה או לפי שהיציאה היתה יתירה על השבח:
notes.en: Due to its inferior quality: either because its tax was great, or because the expense was greater than the yield.

notes.dh: ואמרו לו פתח אתה ראשון ואמר הרי היא שלי באיסר
notes.he: שלא היה מחשבה ביותר מפני רעתה:
notes.en: And they said to him: You open first; and he said: It is hereby mine for an issar: for he did not think it worth more, because of its poor quality.

messages.text: That person did not say he would purchase it for an issar; rather, he said he would purchase it for an egg, as consecrated items may be redeemed with money or with the equivalent value of money.

notes.he: הרי היא שלי בביצה שהקדש נפדה בכסף ובשוה כסף:
notes.en: He did not say “for an issar”; rather: “It is hereby mine for an egg,” for consecrated property is redeemed with money and with the equivalent of money.

notes.he: תימה איך היה זה המעשה בימי ר' יוסי והלא ר' יוסי לא היה בזמן הבית ואם כן לא הוצרך לפתוח תחילה בבעלים וי"ל דפליג על פי הקבלה ע"פ שאירע בזמן הבית א"נ אפי' שלא בזמן הבית גאולה בבעלים תחילה כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ז) אם לא יגאל ונמכר:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei said, and so on: It is puzzling: how could this incident have taken place in the days of Rabbi Yosei? Rabbi Yosei did not live in the time of the Temple, and if so, there was no need to open first with the owners. One can say that he disagrees on the basis of a tradition [he received] that it happened in the time of the Temple. Alternatively, even not in the time of the Temple, redemption is first with the owners, as it is written (Leviticus 27:27): “And if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold.”

notes.dh: אמר רבי יוסי לא כך היה מעשה
notes.he: כלומר שלא אמר הרי היא שלי באיסר אלא הרי היא שלי בביצה. ומכאן אתה למד שהקדש אינו כמעשר שני שאינו נפדה אלא בכסף אלא דהקדש נפדה בכסף ובשוה כסף:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei said: the incident was not so. That is, he did not say “It is hereby mine for an issar” but “It is hereby mine for an egg.” And from here you learn that consecrated property is not like second tithe, which is redeemed only with money; rather, consecrated property is redeemed with money and with the equivalent of money.

messages.text: The treasurer said to him: The field has come into your possession based on your bid. As a result, he loses an issar and his field remains before him in his possession.

notes.he: הגזבר:
notes.en: He said to him: the treasurer [said to him].

notes.he: הרי היא שלך:
notes.en: It has come to you: it is hereby yours.

notes.he: תהא שלך ותן האיסר:
notes.en: They said to him: It has come to you: let it be yours, and give the issar.

notes.he: שנותנו להקדש:
notes.en: He loses an issar: which he gives to the Temple.

notes.he: היא שלו עם רעתה ויש לו ב' הפסדות אחר החזרה אחד שחזרה לו שדהו ואחד שהפסיד האיסר:
notes.en: And his field is before him: it is his, with its poor quality, and he has two losses after the return: one, that his field returned to him; and one, that he lost the issar.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that with regard to one who consecrates his ancestral field during a period when the Jubilee Year is not observed, the treasurer says to him: You open the bidding first. Why does the treasurer merely say this to him? But isn’t it taught in a baraita that the treasurer forces him to open the bidding?
messages.quote: he says to the owner: You open the bidding first

notes.he: את הבעלים לפתוח ראשון:
notes.en: Gemara. But isn’t it taught: they force: the owners to open first.

notes.he: משום (דהוא הקדיש) [ריוח הקדש] כדי שיוסיף חומש:
notes.en: But isn’t it taught: they force: for the sake of the Temple’s profit [the text in parentheses reads “because he consecrated it”], so that he will add a fifth.

messages.text: What is the meaning of the phrase: The treasurer says to him? It means that the treasurer forces him to open the bidding.

notes.he: וא"ת מ"ש דצריך כפיה הכא טפי מכל הני דתנן בסוף פ"ק דבכורות (דף יג.) מצות פדייה קודמת למצות עריפה מצות יעידה קודמת למצות פדייה מצות ייבום קודמת למצות חליצה מצות גאולה באדון קודמת (למצות) לכל אדם ומפיק כולהו מקראי התם ולא אשכחן כפייה כי אם בזה וי"ל דשאני הכא דיכול לבא לידי תקלה אם יהנו העולם ממנה:
notes.en: What is “says”? They force: And if you ask: why is coercion needed here more than in all those that we learned at the end of the first chapter of Bekhorot (13a): the mitzva of redemption takes precedence over the mitzva of breaking the neck; the mitzva of designation takes precedence over the mitzva of redemption; the mitzva of levirate marriage takes precedence over the mitzva of ḥalitza; the mitzva of redemption by the owner takes precedence over anyone else? It derives all of them there from verses, and we do not find coercion except in this one. One can say that here is different, because it can lead to a stumbling block if people derive benefit from it.

messages.text: that initially the treasurer says to him that he should open the bidding; if he complies, he complies; and if not, the treasurer forces him to comply.

The mishna teaches that the one who consecrated the field opens the bidding, as the owner gives an additional one-fifth payment whereas others do not give an additional one-fifth payment. Why does the mishna state that the reason he opens the bidding is specifically because the owner gives an additional one-fifth?
messages.quote: as the owner gives an additional payment of one-fifth

messages.text: Let the tanna derive it from the reason that since the field is dear to the owner he would increase his bid and redeem it for a higher price. And furthermore, doesn’t the mitzva of redemption begin with the owner of the field by Torah law?

notes.he: בפ"ק דבכורות (דף יג.):
notes.en: That the mitzva of redemption is with the owner: in the first chapter of Bekhorot (13a).

notes.he: כלומר לפי שהוא מכירה יותר מאחר כמה היא עושה יוסיף בפדיונה יותר ממי שאינו מכירה:
notes.en: That since it is dear to him he would increase and redeem it: that is, since he knows better than another how much it yields, he will add to its redemption more than one who does not know it.

notes.he: כדתנן בפרק קמא דבכורות מצות גאולה באדון קודמת לכל אדם:
notes.en: And furthermore, the mitzva of redemption is with the owner: as we learned in the first chapter of Bekhorot: the mitzva of redemption by the owner takes precedence over anyone else.

messages.text: The tanna states one reason and there are another two reasons: One reason is that since it is dear to him he would increase his bid and redeem it for a higher price; another reason is that the mitzva of redemption begins with the owner; and another reason is that the owner gives an additional one-fifth payment and every other person does not give an additional one-fifth payment.

notes.he: מוסיף ופודה יותר משאר אדם:
notes.en: He would increase and redeem it: he adds and redeems it for more than other people.

notes.he: דכתיב ואם לא יגאל ונמכר בערכך אלמא מצות גאולה קודמת למכירה:
notes.en: The mitzva of redemption is with the owner: as it is written (Leviticus 27:27): “And if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation”; evidently the mitzva of redemption takes precedence over sale.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: There was an incident involving one who consecrated his field, which was causing him a loss due to its low quality. The treasurers said to him: You open the bidding first. He said: It is hereby mine for an issar. Rabbi Yosei says: That person did not say he would purchase it for an issar; rather, he said he would purchase it for an egg, as consecrated items may be redeemed with money or with the equivalent value of money.
messages.quote: for an egg, as consecrated items may be redeemed with money or with the equivalent value of money

messages.text: Let us say they disagree about this, that Rabbi Yosei holds that the equivalent value of money is the same as money, and the Rabbis hold that the equivalent value of money is not the same as money.
But don’t we maintain as an accepted principle that the equivalent value of money is the same as money?

notes.he: דאמרי' בבבא קמא (דף ז.) ישיב לרבות שוה כסף אפי' סובין:
notes.en: But don’t we maintain that the equivalent of money is like money: as we say in Bava Kamma (7a): “He shall return” — to include the equivalent of money, even bran.

notes.he: והא קי"ל בכל דוכתא דשוה כסף ככסף חוץ ממעשר שני:
notes.en: He states one and another, and so on. And don’t we maintain everywhere that the equivalent of money is like money, except for second tithe?

messages.text: Everyone agrees that the equivalent value of money is the same as money, and here they disagree with regard to whether one may redeem with an item one-fifth of whose value is not worth one peruta.

The first tanna holds that one may redeem with an issar, which is worth eight perutot, as one-fifth of its value is greater than the value of one peruta, and Rabbi Yosei holds that one may even redeem with an item such as an egg, despite the fact that one-fifth of its value is not worth one peruta.

notes.dh: רבי יוסי סבר בכביצה נמי פרקינן
notes.he: ובפ' הזהב (ב"מ דף נג:) איכא פלוגתא איכא מ"ד בו ובחומשו ואיכא מאן דאמר בו אע"ג שאין בחומשו ונראה דכביצה היינו שוה פרוטה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei holds one may redeem even with something like an egg: In the chapter HaZahav (Bava Metzia 53b) there is a dispute: one opinion says [it must be worth a peruta] in itself and in its fifth, and one says in itself, even though not in its fifth. And it seems that “like an egg” means the equivalent of a peruta.

notes.he: אע"ג דאין בחומשה שוה פרוטה:
notes.en: One may redeem even with something like an egg: even though its fifth is not worth a peruta.

messages.text: The mishna relates that after the owner made his bid the treasurer said to him: The field has come into your possession based on your bid. As a result, he loses an issar and his field remains before him in his possession. This statement, whose source is unspecified, is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who hold that in the incident in the mishna, the man redeemed the field with an issar.
messages.quote: he loses an issar and his field remains before him

notes.he: דקתני מפסיד איסר ולא קתני נמצא מפסיד ביצה רבנן היא ולא רבי יוסי:
notes.en: This unspecified [statement]: which teaches “he loses an issar” and does not teach “he is found to lose an egg,” is the Rabbis and not Rabbi Yosei.

notes.he: סתמא כרבנן דאמרי בחומשה בעינן פרוטה [דהיינו ת"ק (ור' דאמרי) [דר"י] דאמר הרי היא שלי באיסר ושמעינן מינה שאין פודין בדבר שאין בחומשו שוה פרוטה]:
notes.en: The unspecified ruling accords with the Rabbis, who say its fifth must be worth a peruta [that is, the first tanna, not Rabbi Yosei, who said “It is hereby mine for an issar”; and we learn from it that one does not redeem with something whose fifth is not worth a peruta].

messages.text: Mishna
If one said: The field is hereby mine for ten sela, and one other person said: It is mine for twenty, and one said for thirty, and one said for forty, and one said for fifty;

notes.he: ואחד אומר בחמשים כשומה של תורה דכתיב בחמשים שקל כסף:
notes.en: And one said for fifty: like the Torah’s valuation, as it is written: “fifty shekels of silver.”

messages.text: and then the one who bid fifty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela and the field is redeemed by the one who bid forty. This ensures that the Temple treasury does not lose.

notes.he: שנתחרט בו:
notes.en: The one of fifty reneged: that he regretted it.

notes.he: כלומר שממשכנין אותו כשיעור אותו תוספת שהוסיף יותר מן האחרים דאמירתו לגבוה כמסירתו להדיוט וכן כולם ממשכנין אותן כשחזרו בהן כשיעור כל אחד מה שהוסיף על חברו:
notes.en: One repossesses from his property up to ten: that is, one takes collateral from him to the measure of the addition that he added beyond the others, since his statement to the Most High is like his delivery to an ordinary person. And likewise all of them: when they renege, one takes collateral from each to the measure of what he added over his fellow.

messages.text: If the one who bid forty sela subsequently reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela and the field is redeemed by the one who bid thirty.

notes.he: נמצא ביד גזבר עשרים וכן שלשים יתן שלשים הרי חמשים:
notes.en: Mishna. One repossesses from his property ten sela: it turns out that the treasurer has twenty in hand [after the bidders of fifty and forty reneged], and so [the bidder of] thirty gives thirty; that makes fifty.

messages.text: If the one who bid thirty subsequently reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela and the field is redeemed by the one who bid twenty. If the one who bid twenty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela and it is redeemed by the one who bid ten.
If the one who bid ten reneged on his offer, the treasurer sells the field at its value and collects the remainder from the property of the one who bid ten, to complete the sum of ten sela.

notes.dh: חזר בו של עשר מוכרין אותה בשוויה
notes.he: ואם לא יכלו למוכרה [בעשר] נפרעין משל עשר את המותר עד שיהא להקדש בה עשר סלעים הואיל וזה שמאה בעשר סלעים:
notes.en: If the one of ten reneged, one sells it at its value; and if they could not sell it [for ten], one collects the remainder from the one of ten until the Temple has ten sela from it, since he assessed it at ten sela.

messages.text: If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and any other person says he will pay twenty sela, the offer of the owner takes precedence, due to the fact that he adds one-fifth.
If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and one other person said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-one sela,

notes.dh: אמר אחד הרי היא שלי בכ"א
notes.he: לאחר שאמרו בעלים בעשרים:
notes.en: One said: It is hereby mine for twenty-one: after the owners said twenty.

messages.text: the owner gives twenty-six sela and takes the field. He pays the twenty that he initially offered; plus five sela, which is one-fifth of the total future sum, i.e., one-quarter of his initial offer. In addition, he adds one sela, the difference between his initial offer and that of the other person, so that the Temple treasury will not receive less than the twenty-one sela offer proposed by the other person.

notes.he: על כרחן:
notes.en: The owners give: against their will.

notes.he: דלהאי לא יהבינן לה הואיל ואמרו בעלים עשרים ועולה החשבון עם החומש לכ"ה ואי יהביה להאיך בכ"א נמצא הקדש מפסיד ובעלים יתנו על כרחן אותו סלע שהוסיף זה על הקרן וכ"ה דידהו אבל על סלע שהוסיף זה לא יוסיפו חומש:
notes.en: Twenty-six: for we do not give it to this one, since the owners said twenty and the reckoning with the fifth comes to twenty-five; and if [the treasurer] gave it to that one for twenty-one, the Temple would be found to lose. So the owners give, against their will, that sela which this one added to the principal, and their own twenty-five; but on the sela that this one added they do not add a fifth.

notes.dh: אמר אחד הרי היא שלי בעשרים ואחד סלעין הבעלים נותנין עשרים ושש
notes.he: לפי שהבעלים אמרו בעשרים ומוסיפין עוד חומש על עשרים הרי כ"ו וכן לעולם כופין הבעלים שיפדוה הן בשביל שמוסיפין חומש ויתנו עוד גם התוספת שמוסיף אחד על העשרים אבל אין מוסיפין הבעלים חומש על אותו עילוי שמעלה אחד על העשרים אלא יתנו התוס' לבדו על חומש שלהן כגון אמר אחד הרי היא שלי בכ"ה הבעלים יתנו ל' ולא יותר חמש בשביל חומש שלהן וחמש בשביל תוספת של זה אבל] אמר אחד הרי היא שלי בכ"ו. אין כופין את הבעלים לפדותה כדאמרינן בגמ' דמצי אמרי אתא גברא בחריקין שהוסיף על הכ' כנגד החומש שאנו חייבין להוסיף מעתה אין אנו חייבין לפדות אא"כ רצו הבעלים עדיין לפדותה:
notes.en: One said: It is hereby mine for twenty-one sela; the owners give twenty-six. For the owners said twenty and add a further fifth on the twenty, making twenty-six [with the other’s added sela]. And so always they force the owners to redeem it themselves, because they add a fifth, and they also give the addition that the other added over twenty. But the owners do not add a fifth on the increase that the other raises over twenty; rather, they give the addition alone on top of their own fifth. For example, if one said “It is hereby mine for twenty-five,” the owners give thirty and no more: five for their fifth and five for this one’s addition. But if one said “It is hereby mine for twenty-six,” they do not force the owners to redeem it, as we say in the Gemara, for they can say “A man has come in our place [baḥarikin],” who added on the twenty the equivalent of the fifth that we were obligated to add; from now on we are not obligated to redeem, unless the owners still wish to redeem it.

messages.text: If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and another person said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-two sela, the owner gives twenty-seven sela and takes the field.

If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and another said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-three sela, the owner gives twenty-eight sela and takes the field. If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and another said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-four sela, the owner gives twenty-nine sela and takes the field.

If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and another said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-five sela, the owner gives thirty sela, as the owner adds one-fifth only to the amount that he bid, and does not add one-fifth to the addition of that other person.

notes.dh: אמר אחד בעשרים וחמש הבעלים נותנים שלשים
notes.he: על כרחן. והשתא איכא למיפרך אמאי כופין את הבעלים בשלמא עד השתא כייפינן להו דהא לא מצינן למיתבה להנך משום דקרן דידהו לא הוי כקרן וחומש דאמור בעלים ברישא הלכך על כרחין הדרינן אבעלים וכיון דהדרינן אבעלים בעי למיתב קרנא כמה דשמאי אחריני וחומשא דידהו אבל השתא דאמר אחד בכ"ה ליתביה להאיך דהא קרן דידיה הוי כקרן וחומש דאמור בעלים ברישא ובגמ' פריך לה:
notes.en: One said twenty-five; the owners give thirty: against their will. And now one could object: why do they force the owners? Granted, until now we force them, since we cannot give it to these others, because their principal is not as much as the principal and fifth that the owners said first; therefore we perforce return to the owners, and since we return to the owners they must give the principal as the others assessed it, and their own fifth. But now that one said twenty-five, let them give it to that one, for his principal equals the principal and fifth that the owners said first. And in the Gemara it raises this objection.

messages.text: If the owner said he will pay twenty sela and one other person said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-six sela, if the owner wished to pay thirty-one sela and a dinar the owner takes precedence;

notes.he: אם רצו ליתן שלשים ואחת ודינר שכך עולה החשבון בין החומש שלהן והתוספת של זה הבעלים קודמין:
notes.en: If they wished to give thirty-one and a dinar: for so the reckoning comes to, between their fifth and this one’s addition; the owners take precedence.

messages.text: and if not, the treasurer says to the other person: The field has come into your possession based on your bid, as it is more than the Temple treasury can compel the owner to pay.

notes.he: שלא רצו הבעלים ליתן כל כך:
notes.en: And if not: that the owners did not wish to give so much.

notes.he: לזה שאמר בכ"ו:
notes.en: He says to him: to this one who said twenty-six.

notes.he: תן מה שאמרת והרי היא שלך:
notes.en: It has come to you: give what you said, and it is yours.

messages.caption: The owner bids twenty sela and another person bids more: what the mishna has the owner pay.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches that if one said: The field is mine for ten sela, and another said for twenty, and another said thirty, and another said forty, and yet another said fifty; and then the one who bid fifty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela, and it is redeemed by the one who bid forty. In this manner, the Temple treasury does not lose.
messages.quote: the one who bid fifty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten

messages.text: The mishna taught that the treasurer repossesses ten sela from the one who initially offered fifty sela only when the one who offered forty stands in his place and intends to purchase the field, as the Temple treasury would have lost only ten sela.

notes.he: דאין ממשכנין מנכסי בן חמשים אלא עשר סלעים אלא שבן מ' במקומו עומד ואינו חוזר בו אבל חזר בו בן ארבעים משלשין הכ' סלעים הפחותין מנ' ועד שלשים ביניהם דבן נ' יתן ט"ו ובן מ' יתן ה' דהא באותן עשר שאמר בן נ' יותר על בן מ' לא שייך בר מ' בהדיה בפסידא והנך י' שהוסיף בן מ' על בר ל' בר חמשין נמי אירצי במ' דיש בכלל חמשים ארבעים:
notes.en: Gemara. They taught only: that one repossesses from the property of the bidder of fifty only ten sela, when the bidder of forty stands in his place and does not renege. But if the bidder of forty reneged, they divide the twenty sela [lost] between fifty and thirty between them: the bidder of fifty gives fifteen and the bidder of forty gives five. For in the ten that the bidder of fifty said beyond the bidder of forty, the bidder of forty has no share in the loss with him; but the ten that the bidder of forty added over the bidder of thirty, the bidder of fifty also agreed to, along with the forty, since forty is included in fifty.

notes.he: דאמרי דכי חזר בו של חמשים דממשכנין מנכסיו עד עשר ולא יותר אלא דבן ארבעים עומד במקומו שאינו משלשין ביניהם שעכשיו נפחתו להקדש י' שקלים:
notes.en: They taught only: that when the one of fifty reneged, one repossesses from his property up to ten and no more, only when the bidder of forty stands in his place, so that they do not divide between them, since now the Temple has been reduced by ten shekels.

messages.text: But if the one who offered forty does not stand in his place, i.e., he too reneged on his offer, then the additional amount they had offered is divided between the one who initially offered fifty and the one who offered forty, as follows:

notes.he: משלשין ביניהן זה הפיחות שיתן בן חמשים ט"ו שקל ובן מ' יתן ה' שקל:
notes.en: They divide this reduction between them: the bidder of fifty gives fifteen shekels and the bidder of forty gives five shekels.

messages.text: The one who offered fifty pays all ten of the difference between fifty and forty, but he must also pay half of the extra ten that is the difference between the offer of forty and the previous offer of thirty. The reason is that the one who bid fifty agreed to that extra ten that raised the price from thirty to forty. In sum, the one who offered fifty pays fifteen, and the one who said forty pays five.

notes.he: מ"ט האי בן חמשים העשר שהוא הוסיף יתן הוא לבדו בלא דין ודברים והעשר שקל שהוסיף בן מ' על בן ל' יאמר בן מ' לבן נ' את נמי שייך בהדיה (בני) עשר דידי דיש בכלל חמשים הני ארבעים הילכך יהיב נמי פלגא דהני עשר ואידך הי' שקלים יתן לחוד דליכא בן חמשים אחר שלא שמאה שום אדם בחמשים:
notes.en: What is the reason? This bidder of fifty gives the ten that he added by himself, without dispute. And as for the ten shekels that the bidder of forty added over the bidder of thirty, the bidder of forty says to the bidder of fifty: You too share with me in my ten, since these forty are included in fifty. Therefore he gives half of these ten as well. And the other ten shekels he gives alone, since there is no other bidder of fifty, for no one else assessed it at fifty.

messages.text: An objection is raised to the statement of Rav Ḥisda from that which we learned in the mishna: If the one who bid forty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela.
messages.quote: If the one who bid forty sela subsequently reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten

messages.text: According to Rav Ḥisda, there is a difficulty: Why does the mishna rule that his property is repossessed by ten sela? Let the one who offered fifty give together with him, and therefore the one who offered forty should give only five.
The mishna is referring to a case where there is no one who offered fifty sela.

notes.he: שלא אמר אדם יותר על מ' דמתני' מילי מילי קתני:
notes.en: Where there is no bidder of fifty: that no one said more than forty, for the mishna teaches case by case.

messages.text: The mishna also teaches that if the one who bid thirty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela. But according to Rav Ḥisda, why is only his property repossessed? Let the one who offered forty give together with him.
messages.quote: If the one who bid thirty subsequently reneged on his offer

notes.he: ליתן הבן ארבעים ט"ו דליתשיך בפלגא דהני עשר דבן שלשים:
notes.en: Let the bidder of forty give fifteen, so that he is drawn in for half of these ten of the bidder of thirty.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case where there is no one who offered forty sela.

notes.he: אי איכא בן ארבעים הכי נמי אלא דליכא בן ארבעים הילכך יהיב בן שלשים עשר:
notes.en: If there is a bidder of forty, so indeed; but [this is] where there is no bidder of forty; therefore the bidder of thirty gives ten.

messages.text: The mishna states that if the one who bid twenty reneged on his offer, the treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela. According to Rav Ḥisda, why is only his property repossessed? Let the one who offered thirty give together with him.
The mishna is referring to a case where there is no one who offered thirty sela.

If so, then say the latter clause of the mishna: If the one who bid ten reneged on his offer, the treasurer sells the field at its value and collects the remainder from the property of the one who bid ten, to complete the sum of ten sela. Why is payment collected only from the one who offered ten? Let the one who offered twenty give together with him.
messages.quote: If the one who bid ten reneged on his offer, the treasurer sells the field at its value

notes.he: כדאמר רב חסדא:
notes.en: If so: as Rav Ḥisda said.

notes.he: אימא סיפא חזר בו של עשר כו':
notes.en: Say the latter clause: the one of ten reneged, and so on.

notes.he: דאיהו נמי בעשר אירצי:
notes.en: Let the bidder of twenty give with him: for he too agreed to ten.

messages.text: And if you would say that here too, there is no one who offered twenty sela, then if so, why does the mishna state: And collects from the one who bid ten? The mishna should have stated simply: And collects from him, as there is no one else who submitted an offer.

notes.he: ] מדקתני משל י' מכלל דאיכא אחרינא:
notes.en: From the one of ten: since it teaches “from the one of ten,” this implies that there is another.

notes.he: אי דליכא אלא עשר [לחודיה] אמאי איצטריך למימר נפרעין משל עשר נפרעין ממנו מבעי ליה. אלא מדקתני נפרעין משל עשר ש"מ דאיכא נמי של בן עשרים ולא קתני משלשין ביניהם וקשיא לרב חסדא:
notes.en: If so: if there is only [the bidder of] ten [alone], why did it need to say “one collects from the one of ten”? It should have said “one collects from him.” Rather, since it teaches “one collects from the one of ten,” conclude from it that there is also a bidder of twenty, and it does not teach that they divide between them; and it is difficult for Rav Ḥisda.

messages.text: This is not difficult. Here, when the potential loss incurred by the Temple treasury is divided, they reneged on their offers simultaneously; whereas there, in the mishna, where only one individual must cover the loss, two individuals reneged one after the other.

notes.he: אלא לא קשיא כאן שחזרו כולן בבת אחת משלשין [ביניהן] אבל חזרו בזה אחר זה נפרעין מכל אחד תוספתו:
notes.en: Rather, it is not difficult: here, where all of them reneged at once, they divide [between them]; but where they reneged one after another, one collects from each his own addition.

messages.text: This is also taught in a baraita:
If all of them reneged at once they divide the potential loss incurred by the Temple treasury between them.

notes.dh: חזרו בהן בבת אחת משלשין ביניהן
notes.he: כדרב חסדא ומתני' כגון שחזרו בהן בזה אחר זה דהשתא אמר בן נ' לגזבר כי הדרי בי שבקי לך בר מ':
notes.en: If they reneged all at once they divide between them: as Rav Ḥisda [said]; and the mishna is where they reneged one after another, for then the bidder of fifty says to the treasurer: When I reneged, I left you the bidder of forty.

notes.he: שנים ושלשה ראשונים נשכרין ושנים אחרונים נפסדין שאם חזרו כולם ומכרה גזבר בשוויה חמש סלעים נמצאו פחותין מ"ה סלעים יתן בן נ' הי' שלו לבדו ומעשר של בן מ' יתן החצי ששניהם נתרצו בהן ומעשר של בן שלשים יתן השליש ובן מ' השליש ובן שלשים השליש ששלשתן שלשים אמרו והעשר של בן עשרים יתנו בין ארבעתם והחמש שפחתו מבן עשר יתנו חמשתן:
notes.en: They divide between them: the first ones gain and the last two lose [the printed text reads “two and three first ones gain and two last ones lose”: compared with reneging one after another, those who bid first (10, 20, 30) pay less and the last two (40, 50) pay more]. For if all of them reneged and the treasurer sold it at its value, [say] five sela, there is a shortfall of forty-five sela. The bidder of fifty gives the ten that are his alone. Of the ten of the bidder of forty, he gives half, for both of them agreed to them. Of the ten of the bidder of thirty, the bidder of fifty gives a third, the bidder of forty a third and the bidder of thirty a third, for all three of them said thirty. The ten of the bidder of twenty, all four of them give between them. And the five by which [the sale] fell short of the bidder of ten, all five of them give.

notes.he: דכי חזרו כולן כאחד משלשין ביניהן כיצד של חמשים יתן ט"ו ושל ארבעים ה' מתוספתו וה' [מתוספת] בן שלשים ובן שלשים יתן חצי תוספתו [וחצי תוספתו מבן כ' ובן כ' יתן חצי תוספתו] וחצי מן המותר שנפרעין מבן עשר:
notes.en: This is also taught: that when all reneged together they divide between them. How? The one of fifty gives fifteen; the one of forty gives five of his addition and five [of the addition] of the bidder of thirty; the bidder of thirty gives half his addition [and half of the addition of the bidder of twenty; and the bidder of twenty gives half his addition] and half of the remainder that is collected from the bidder of ten.

messages.text: Now didn’t we learn in the mishna: The treasurer repossesses from his property up to ten sela, without any mention of a division? Rather, must one not conclude from the baraita that the halakha is in accordance with the statement of Rav Ḥisda, who holds that when two individuals renege on their offers simultaneously they divide the loss between them?

notes.he: [והאנן תנן ממשכנין מנכסי של כל אחד עד עשר אלא לאו ש"מ כדרב חסדא כדמתרצינן כאן בבת אחת כאן בזה אחר זה:
notes.en: But didn’t we learn: one repossesses from the property of each one up to ten? Rather, must one not conclude from it as Rav Ḥisda, as we resolved: here at once, there one after another?

messages.text: Indeed, conclude from it that this is the case.

messages.caption: Bidders who renege: one after the other, as in the mishna; fifty and forty together, as Rav Ḥisda divides it; and all five at once, as Rashi works it out.

messages.text: There are those who raise this baraita as a contradiction:

notes.he: ולא תני להא דרב חסדא באנפי נפשה אלא ע"י תירוץ דמתני' וברייתא דרמו אהדדי:
notes.en: Some raise them as a contradiction: and they do not teach this [statement] of Rav Ḥisda on its own, but only by way of resolving the mishna and the baraita that contradict each other.

messages.text: We learned in the mishna that if the one who bid ten reneged on his offer, the treasurer sells the field at its value and collects the remainder from the property of the one who bid ten. But isn’t it taught in a baraita that they divide the potential loss to the Temple treasury between them?
This is not difficult. Here in the baraita they reneged on their offers simultaneously, whereas there, in the mishna, two individuals reneged one after the other.

§ The mishna teaches: If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and any other person says he will pay twenty sela, the owner’s offer takes precedence because he adds one-fifth. Is this to say that an offer of the owner, which perforce includes an additional one-fifth, is preferable to a higher offer for the principal submitted by another?
messages.quote: the owner takes precedence, due to the fact that he adds one-fifth

notes.dh: למימרא דחומש עדיף ורמינהי בעל הבית אומר בסלע
notes.he: תימה לר' אלחנן מאי פריך דהא ליכא למיפרך דהבעלים אומרים בעשרים וכל אדם בעשרים הבעלים קודמים כו' והכא תניא דאחר קודם ומאי קושיא דהא דהבעלים קודמין זהו כשאין אחר פודהו ביותר ומסיפא נמי ליכא למיפרך דתניא אחד אומר הרי הוא שלי בעשרים ואחד הבעלים קודמין ונותן כ"ו והכא תניא דאחר קודם הכי נמי לא קשיא דמידי הוא טעמא אלא מפני שמוסיף על הקרן שהוא עשרים ה"נ במתני' דין הוא שיקדמו הבעלים שגם הם מוסיפין על הקרן כשנותנין עשרים ושש שנותנין האחד יותר על העשרים והחומש בשביל (חומש) הקרן שהוא עשרים ואחת ושמא הוא מקשה כך מאי שנא שכופין הבעלים לתת דמים שאמר האחר וחומשו על מה שאמר הוא דקתני שהבעלים נותנין כ"ו כ"ז והכא תניא כשהבעלים אומרים בסלע והאחר אומר בסלע ואיסר [של סלע ואיסר] קודם ואין אנו כופין את הבעלים שיתנו סלע ואיסר עם החומש דקתני של סלע ואיסר קודם ולא קתני הבעלים נותנין חמשה דינרים שהוא קרן וחומש ואיסר ומשני הכא חומשא רווחא דהקדש חומש עדיף הלכך כופין את הבעלים התם דחומשא רווחא דבעל הבית כו':
notes.en: Is this to say that the fifth is preferable? And raise a contradiction: the householder says: for a sela: Rabbi Elḥanan found it puzzling: what is the objection? One cannot object from [the clause] “the owners say twenty and anyone says twenty, the owners take precedence,” while here it is taught that the other takes precedence — what difficulty is that? For the owners take precedence only when no other redeems it for more. Nor can one object from the latter clause, where it is taught: one said “It is hereby mine for twenty-one,” the owners take precedence and give twenty-six, while here it is taught that the other takes precedence. That too is not difficult: for the reason [there] is only that he adds to the principal, which is twenty; so too in our mishna it is right that the owners take precedence, since they too add to the principal when they give twenty-six, for they give the one beyond the twenty, and the fifth on account of the principal, [so that the principal] is twenty-one. Perhaps, then, he objects thus: why is it different here, that the owners are forced to give the sum the other said, and the fifth on what [the owner] himself said, as it teaches “the owners give twenty-six, twenty-seven”; whereas there it is taught that when the householder says “for a sela” and the other says “for a sela and an issar,” [the one of a sela and an issar] takes precedence, and we do not force the householder to give a sela and an issar with the fifth? For it teaches “the one of a sela and an issar takes precedence,” and does not teach “the householder gives five dinars,” which is principal and fifth, and an issar. And it answers: here, the fifth is the Temple’s gain, so the fifth is preferable, and therefore we force the owners; there, the fifth is the householder’s gain, and so on.

messages.text: And it raises a contradiction from a mishna (Ma’aser Sheni 4:3):

If one is unable to transport his second-tithe produce to Jerusalem to consume it there, the produce is redeemed and the redemption money is spent on food in Jerusalem. If the owner of second tithe says he will redeem it for one sela and one other says he will redeem it for one sela and one issar, the offer of one sela and one issar takes precedence, because he adds to the principal.

notes.he: ] בעה"ב הפודה מעשר שני שלו מוסיף חומש דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ל״א) ואם גאל יגאל איש ממעשרו וגו' ואחר הפודה אין מוסיף חומש. בעה"ב אומר בסלע ואחר אומר בסלע ואיסר כו' שמוסיף על הקרן ואע"ג דבעל הבית בעי למיתב טפי דחומש סלע הוי דינר ודינר הוי עשרים וד' איסרין בפ"ק דקדושין (דף יב.):
notes.en: [The householder says: for a sela:] A householder who redeems his own second tithe adds a fifth, as it is written (Leviticus 27:31): “And if a man will redeem any of his tithe,” and so on; and another who redeems it does not add a fifth. The householder says “for a sela” and another says “for a sela and an issar,” and so on: [the latter takes precedence] because he adds to the principal, even though the householder would have to give more, since a fifth of a sela is a dinar, and a dinar is twenty-four issarin, [as stated] in the first chapter of Kiddushin (12a).

notes.he: לפדות מעשר שני שלו בסלע ואחד אומר תנהו לי ואני אתן בשבילו סלע ואיסר קודם של סלע ואיסר לבעל הבית ויהיה המעשר שלו מפני שמוסיף על הקרן איסר יותר מבעה"ב ואע"ג דכי פריק ליה בעה"ב מחוייב להוסיף חומש כדכתיב ואם גאל יגאל איש ממעשרו חמשיתו יוסף עליו ואחר אין מוסיף חומש אפי' הכי של סלע ואיסר קודם לבעה"ב:
notes.en: And the householder says: to redeem his second tithe for a sela, and another says: Give it to me and I will give a sela and an issar for it. The one of a sela and an issar takes precedence over the householder, and the tithe will be his, because he adds an issar to the principal beyond the householder. And even though, when the householder redeems it, he is obligated to add a fifth, as it is written: “And if a man will redeem any of his tithe, he shall add to it the fifth part thereof,” and another does not add a fifth, even so the one of a sela and an issar takes precedence over the householder.

messages.text: Here, where the additional one-fifth is a gain of the Temple treasury, a calculation that includes the one-fifth is preferable.

notes.he: ומתרץ לא קשיא דהכא בגואל שדהו דחומש דמוסיפין בעלים רווחא דהקדש הוא שהקרן והחומש בא ליד הגזבר משום הכי ההוא דיהיב חומש להקדש עדיף:
notes.en: And it answers: it is not difficult. For here, with one who redeems his field, the fifth that the owners add is the Temple’s gain, since principal and fifth come into the treasurer’s hand; therefore the one who gives a fifth to the Temple is preferable.

messages.text: By contrast, there, where the additional one-fifth belongs to the owner, i.e., the Temple treasury gains nothing from it, as the redemption money for second-tithe produce belongs to the owner and must be taken to Jerusalem for him to spend it there, let the principal be redeemed for a proper sum, and we do not care about the additional one-fifth.

notes.he: גבי מעשר שני חומש רווחא דבעל הבית הוא שהרי בין קרן בין חומש הכל שלו והוא יאכל הכל בירושלים ואין לנו בו אלא מצות פדייה שלא יאכלנו בגבולין בלא פדיון ועיקר פדייתו בקרן היא ואע"ג דבצרי דמי לא איכפת לן שהרי ביתירות דמיו אין נהנה אלא הוא:
notes.en: There: with regard to second tithe, the fifth is the householder’s gain, for both principal and fifth are all his, and he will eat it all in Jerusalem. We have in it only the mitzva of redemption, that he not eat it in the outlying areas without redemption, and the essence of its redemption is with the principal. And even though the money is less, we do not care, since only he benefits from the extra money.

notes.he: גבי מעשר שני דחומשא שמוסיף רווחא דבעה"ב הוא שהקרן והחומש של בעה"ב הוא ומעלהו ואוכלו בירושלים בתורת מעשר וכשמוסיף חומש זהו ריוח שלו שיש לו יותר מעות ממה לקנות כל צורכו בירושלם משו"ה ההוא דפריק הקרן שפיר שמוסיף בפדייתו יותר מבעה"ב איסר הוא קודם לבעה"ב ואע"פ שהבעל הבית מוסיף חומש כיון שאינו בא ליד הקדש לא הקרן ולא החומש אלא ליד בעה"ב לית לן בה בההוא חומש אלא ההוא דפריק קרנא שפיר טפי מחבריה איהו קדים:
notes.en: Here [there]: with second tithe, the fifth he adds is the householder’s gain, for the principal and fifth belong to the householder, and he brings it up and eats it in Jerusalem as tithe; and when he adds a fifth, this is his gain, that he has more money with which to buy all his needs in Jerusalem. Therefore the one who redeems the principal properly, adding an issar more than the householder in its redemption, takes precedence over the householder, even though the householder adds a fifth. Since neither the principal nor the fifth comes into the Temple’s hand, but into the householder’s hand, we do not care about that fifth; rather, the one who redeems the principal better than his fellow takes precedence.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that if the owner says he will pay twenty sela and one other person said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-five sela, the owner gives thirty sela.
messages.quote: of twenty-five sela, the owner gives thirty sela

messages.text: And let the owner say: A man has come in my place [baḥarikin] to redeem the field, as even when accounting for the one-fifth that I must add, my offer stands at twenty-five sela, identical to this man’s offer. Why, then, am I forced to redeem the field for a greater sum?

notes.he: במקומינו שרוצה ליתן כמותינו בשלמא עד השתא הדריתו עלן משום פסידא דהקדש אבל השתא אמאי בעיתו למיכפיין:
notes.en: And let the owners say: A man has come in our place [baḥarikin]: who wants to give as much as we. Granted, until now you came back to us because of the Temple’s loss; but now, why do you want to force us?

notes.he: ואמאי הבעלים נותנין שלשים ולימרו בעלים כבר אתא גברא בהריקין במקומינו שרוצה ליתן כנגד הקרן והחומש שלנו ומעתה נפטרנו:
notes.en: And why do the owners give thirty? Let the owners say: A man has already come in our place [baḥarikin], who wants to give as much as our principal and fifth, and from now on we are exempt.

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case where the owner initially said he would pay twenty sela and an additional dinar, one-quarter of one sela. When the additional one-fifth is taken into account, the owner’s offer is greater than twenty-five sela.

notes.he: ברישא דינר יותר על עשרים דמטי חושבנא דקרן וחומש לכ"ה ודינר ואי יהבינן להאי איכא פסידא להקדש הלכך הדרינן אבעלים על כרחייהו:
notes.en: Where the owners said: at the outset, a dinar more than twenty, so that the reckoning of principal and fifth reaches twenty-five and a dinar; and if we gave it to this one, the Temple would lose. Therefore we return to the owners against their will.

notes.he: לא מצו למימר הכי כגון דאמור בעלים בעשרים ודינר דחייבין ליתן כ"ה ודינר והאי גברא לא אמר אלא כ"ה הלכך ליכא למימר אתא גברא בהריקין:
notes.en: No: they cannot say this, as where the owners said twenty and a dinar, they are obligated to give twenty-five and a dinar, and this man said only twenty-five; therefore one cannot say “A man has come in our place.”

messages.text: But if so, let the mishna teach explicitly that he offered an additional dinar.

notes.he: ברישא דמתני' הבעלים אומרים בעשרים ודינר:
notes.en: And let it teach: in the first clause of the mishna: the owners say twenty and a dinar.

notes.he: אי הכי אמאי לא תני בעלים אומרים עשרים ודינר ליתני דינר:
notes.en: If so, why does it not teach “the owners say twenty and a dinar”? Let it teach a dinar.

messages.text: The tanna was not meticulous with regard to the mention of small sums of money such as one dinar.

notes.he: למתני דינר אלא חשבון הסלעים:
notes.en: It is not meticulous: to teach a dinar, only the reckoning of sela’im.

notes.he: [תנא] דלא רצה לשנות (לבר) [דינר] שהוא פחות משקל:
notes.en: It is not meticulous: the tanna did not want to teach a dinar, which is less than a shekel.

messages.text: And was the tanna not meticulous? But isn’t it taught in the mishna that in a case where one said: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-six sela, if the owner wished to pay thirty-one sela and a dinar the owner takes precedence?
messages.quote: if the owner wished to pay thirty-one sela and a dinar the owner takes precedence

notes.he: דינר בסיפא אלמא דק בדינרין:
notes.en: But it teaches: a dinar in the latter clause; evidently it is meticulous about dinars.

notes.he: [ולא והקתני בסיפא דינר:
notes.en: And is it not [meticulous]? But it teaches a dinar in the latter clause!

messages.text: The mishna is referring to a case where the owner said he would redeem it for twenty sela and one peruta, and the tanna was not meticulous with regard to mentioning such a tiny sum.

notes.he: ברישא פרוטה ובפרוטות לא דק:
notes.en: Rather, Rava said: where the owners said at the outset [twenty and] a peruta; and about perutot it is not meticulous.

notes.he: כגון דאמור בעלים בעשרים ופרוטה דחייבין ליתן כ"ה ופרוטה ואידך גברא לא אמר אלא בכ"ה לחוד ולא מצי למימר אתא גברא בהריקין. וכיון דאמרי בעלים פרוטה ופרוטה לא הוי דבר חשוב ולא רצה התנא לשנותה:
notes.en: Rather, Rava said: where the owners said twenty and a peruta, they are obligated to give twenty-five and a peruta, and the other man said only twenty-five alone, and he cannot say “A man has come in our place.” And since the owners said a peruta, and a peruta is not a significant thing, the tanna did not want to teach it.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that even when the owner must give the amount offered by the second person for the field, he adds one-fifth only to the amount that he himself bid, as he does not add one-fifth to the addition of the other person.
messages.quote: does not add one-fifth to the addition of that other person

messages.text: The mishna taught that the owner does not add one-fifth to the addition of the other person only when the consecrated property was not appraised by three people.

notes.he: שלא שמו שלשה בני אדם את הקרקע כמה שאמר זה האחר:
notes.en: That the consecrated property was not appraised by three: that three people did not appraise the land at what this other one said.

notes.he: דאין מוסיפין חומש על עילוי של זה אלא שלא נישום הקדש בג' בני אדם:
notes.en: They taught only: that one does not add a fifth on this one’s increase only when the consecrated property was not appraised by three people.

messages.text: But if the consecrated property was appraised by three people, and the field was found to be worth the amount offered by the other person, the owner does add one-fifth to the addition of the other person.

notes.he: שמאוה שלשה כדבריו של זה מוסיפין בעלים חומש על עילויו בעל כרחו ולא בעינן עשרה. ואע"ג דשומא דהקדש בעי עשרה כדאמרינן בסנהדרין (דף ב.) הקרקעות תשעה וכהן הכא רבותא קא משמע לן דכיון דאמרי תלתא לא מהדרינן אעשרה ויוסיפו חומש על העילוי:
notes.en: But: if three appraised it according to this one’s words, the owners add a fifth on his increase against their will, and we do not require ten. And even though the appraisal of consecrated property requires ten, as we say in Sanhedrin (2a): land, nine and a priest, here it teaches us a novelty: since three said so, we do not go back to [look for] ten, and they add a fifth on the increase.

notes.he: אם שמאה אותו אחר לדעת ג' בני אדם ששוה כך וכך על עשרים מוסיפין הבעלים נמי חומש אף על אותו עילוי:
notes.en: But: if that other one appraised it with the judgment of three people, that it is worth such and such above twenty, the owners also add a fifth even on that increase.

messages.text: This is also taught in a baraita:

notes.he: ה"ג וכן כתוב בספר ר"ת ול"ג תניא נמי הכי ואי גרסי' ליה יש לפרשו כן תניא נמי הכי דאיכא מאן דסבר דמוסיפין בנישום אי כב"ש אי כב"ה ומדקדק הש"ס למצוא אליבא דרב חסדא ומיהו נראה יותר דגרס תניא בלא נמי הכי:
notes.en: It is taught: Beit Shammai say they add: This is how we read it, and so it is written in the book of Rabbeinu Tam; and we do not read “this is also taught.” And if we do read it, it can be explained thus: “this is also taught,” that there is one who holds that they add [the fifth] when it was appraised, whether according to Beit Shammai or according to Beit Hillel, and the Gemara is exacting to find [this] in accordance with Rav Ḥisda. But it seems more likely that one reads “it is taught,” without “also.”

notes.he: תניא נמי הכי כו']:
notes.en: This is also taught, and so on.

messages.text: Beit Shammai say the owner adds one-fifth to the addition of the other person and Beit Hillel say the owner does not add that one-fifth.

What are the circumstances of this baraita? If it is discussing a case where the field was not appraised by three people, then what is the reasoning of Beit Shammai for their ruling that the owner must add one-fifth to the addition of the other person?
messages.quote: Beit Shammai say the owner adds one-fifth to the addition of the other person

messages.text: Rather, the baraita must be referring to a case where the field was appraised by three people and the appraisal matched the offer of the other person. The owner must therefore add one-fifth to the addition of that other person.

Shall we say that Rav Ḥisda says his statement in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai? This is difficult, as there is a principle that the halakha is ruled in accordance with the opinion of Beit Hillel.
messages.quote: only when the consecrated property was not appraised by three people

messages.text: Actually, the baraita is referring to a case where the field was not appraised by three people, and Beit Shammai are stringent and rule that the owner must nevertheless add one-fifth to the addition of the other person. Rav Ḥisda rules in accordance with the opinion of Beit Hillel that the owner adds one-fifth to the addition of the other person only when the field was appraised by three people.

notes.he: הא נישום אפי' ב"ה מודו דמוסיפין. (וא"כ) [ודקשיא לך] מ"ט דב"ש דאמרי מוסיפין:
notes.en: Actually, where it was not appraised; but where it was appraised, even Beit Hillel agree that they add. And as for what is difficult for you: what is the reason of Beit Shammai, who say they add?

messages.text: Actually, the baraita is referring to a case where the field was appraised by three people and the appraisal matched the offer of the other person; and one should reverse the opinions, i.e., Beit Shammai say that even in such a case the owner does not add one-fifth to the addition of the other person.

notes.he: משום חומרא בעלמא הוא דקאמרי הכי (כיון דאמרת) ואיב"א דנישום ואיפוך ורב חסדא כב"ה דאמרי מוסיפין:
notes.en: Beit Shammai are stringent: they say so merely as a stringency. And if you wish, say: where it was appraised, and reverse [the opinions]; and Rav Ḥisda is like Beit Hillel, who [then] say they add.

messages.text: But according to this interpretation, let the dispute be taught alongside the other rare instances of leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel (see tractate Eduyyot, chapters 4 and 5). Yet, this dispute does not appear there.

notes.he: ששה דברים מקולי ב"ש ומחומרי בית הלל:
notes.en: Six matters are among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel.

messages.text: Rather, one must accept the previous answer, that the baraita is actually discussing a case where the field was not appraised by three people, and Beit Shammai are stringent.

notes.dh: א"כ דב"ה מחמירי דאמרי מוסיפין חומש על עילוי ליתנייה גבי קולי ב"ש וחומרי ב"ה
notes.he: אלא לעולם כדאמרינן מעיקרא דלא נישום [ואפי' הכי ב"ש מחמרי דאמרי מוסיפין] אבל נישום אפי' ב"ה סברי דמוסיפין ורב חסדא דאמר (אפי') כב"ה:
notes.en: If so, that Beit Hillel are stringent in saying they add a fifth on the increase, let it be taught among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel. Rather, actually, as we said at first: where it was not appraised [and even so Beit Shammai are stringent in saying they add]; but where it was appraised, even Beit Hillel hold that they add; and Rav Ḥisda speaks as Beit Hillel.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that in a case where the owner offers to pay twenty sela and one other person said: The field is hereby mine for twenty-six sela, if the owner wished to pay thirty-one sela and a dinar, the owner takes precedence.
messages.quote: if the owner wished to pay thirty-one sela and a dinar the owner takes precedence

messages.text: If the owner wished to pay the additional sum, then yes, he redeems the field, but if the owner did not wish to do so, no, he is not forced to redeem it.

notes.he: [דאין כופין אותן] מ"ט דמצי אמרי אתא גברא בהריקין:
notes.en: If they wished, yes; if they did not wish, no: [for one does not force them]. What is the reason? For they can say: A man has come in our place.

messages.text: The reason is that the owner can say: A man has come in my place to redeem the field for a higher sum, since even when accounting for the additional one-fifth that I must give, my offer amounts to a total of only twenty-five sela, whereas this other person has offered to pay twenty-six. Nevertheless, if the owner chooses to redeem the field, he gives the other person’s offer, twenty-six sela, plus an additional one-fifth of his initial offer, for a total of thirty-one sela.
And the additional dinar that the owner gives, what is its purpose?

notes.he: הא אמרת אין מוסיפין חומש על עילויו של זה:
notes.en: And the dinar, what is its purpose? But you said that one does not add a fifth on this one’s increase!

notes.he: הא [כבר תנא] (אמרת) דאין מוסיפין חומש על עילוי של זה והאי דינר מיחזי כחומש מן ההוא (סלע) [דינר] ששי שעל עשרים:
notes.en: That dinar, what is its purpose? [It has already been taught] that one does not add a fifth on this one’s increase, and this dinar looks like a fifth of that sixth [sela] above twenty.

messages.text: This is what the mishna is saying: If the owner wished from the outset to give based on a calculation that reaches thirty-one sela and one dinar, the owner takes precedence.

notes.he: בשפתחו ראשון:
notes.en: At the outset: when they opened first.

notes.he: על עילויו של זה לשלשים ואחד ודינר:
notes.en: To give a reckoning that reaches: beyond this one’s increase, to thirty-one and a dinar.

notes.he: כיון שאמר בעלים הרי היא שלי בכ"א קודם שאמר זה ועכשיו מגיע להן ליתן בין קרן וחומש כ"ו שקלים ודינר אם רצו ליתן כך הן הבעלים קודמין:
notes.en: Rav Sheshet said this is what it is saying: since the owners said “It is hereby mine for twenty-one” before this one spoke, and now they must give, between principal and fifth, twenty-six shekels and a dinar; if they wish to give so, the owners take precedence.

messages.text: Continues on 28a: Rav Sheshet explains that the owner had first bid twenty-one sela, so that with his fifth he offered twenty-six sela and a dinar, more than the other’s twenty-six; then he takes precedence. If not, the treasurer says to the other: It has come to you.
